1	# claudinite-growth
2	
3	Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
4	lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
5	Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
6	existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.
7	
8	This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
9	lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
10	**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
11	that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.
12	
13	Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
14	scheduler (`packs/claudinite-tasks/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:
15	
16	| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
19	| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | weekly, when the canon or the project's local packs moved in the week | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
20	| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
21	| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | weekly (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |
22	| `rule-revalidation` ([tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md](tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md)) | weekly | a reviewed PR correcting rules whose environment claim no longer probes true |
23	
24	(Plus two agentless tasks over the conversation-logs branch: [usage-fold](../claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/README.md) hourly,
25	described below, and `logs-prune` — retention, [tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs](tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs).)
26	
27	## Extraction is one task over two sources
28	
29	`growth-extract` is the whole capture stage, and it runs **three skills** in order:
30	
31	1. [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) over the window's commits, merged
32	   PRs and issue discussion;
33	2. [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) over the logs captured
34	   from working sessions;
35	3. [prose-to-checks](skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) over the prose **that run just wrote**, to see
36	   whether any of it upgrades to a check before the PR opens.
37	
38	Everything lands in **one** PR, delivered to land where the repo's delivery settings allow
39	(`packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md`). The two extraction halves used to be two tasks firing in
40	the same nightly anchor against the same local packs; they share the lesson bar, the promotion ladder
41	and the dedup surface ([extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)), so the split bought nothing
42	and cost a second opus dispatch, a second PR, and two runs deduping against a corpus the other was
43	concurrently writing.
44	
45	The third step is why the standing `prose-to-checks-sweep` is **weekly**: fresh prose is already
46	offered a conversion the night it is written, so what the sweep sees is a backlog that moves on a
47	weekly clock.
48	
49	A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
50	promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "claudinite-growth", "config": { "promote": false } }`
51	— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).
52	
53	## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in the daily task, retention
54	
55	The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions**, replacing the old in-session post-merge
56	lessons pass. Capture and extraction split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session
57	transcript, so it runs in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only
58	reads the already-pushed logs, so it is the conversation half of the ordinary `growth-extract`
59	scheduled task — the logs branch is *in the repo*, so reading it, committing lessons to local packs,
60	and pruning are plain local git on the working tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the
61	GitHub MCP tools.
62	
63	1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
64	   Right after a merge lands:
65	   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
66	   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
67	   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
68	   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
69	   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
70	   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
71	   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
72	   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
73	   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
74	   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
75	   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
76	   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
77	   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
78	   on, so `test/pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
79	   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
80	   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
81	1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
82	   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
83	   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
84	   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
85	   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
86	   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
87	   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that
88	   do. **Best effort:** a container reclaimed by timeout never fires it, so nothing depends on it
89	   having run — every firing enriches the record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only
90	   behaviour. An `issue-0` log has no issue for the extract to post its exchange
91	   summary on; nothing else about its lifecycle differs.
92	   **Unattended sessions capture through the same step, deliberately not through the hook.** A
93	   scheduled task's executor session ends by having its container reclaimed, which is exactly
94	   the ending no `SessionEnd` fires on — so the executor runs the engine's runner itself as its
95	   last step and names its work item in `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE`, which this step uses in
96	   place of `0`. Those logs therefore file under the task that ran (the item's title
97	   names `pack/task`), and the work no human watched becomes as countable as the work one did.
98	2. **The pass — the conversation half of [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)**
99	   (precondition: a substantive merge; local git on the repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It
100	   applies the [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) skill (the
101	   friction signals and the measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and
102	   token usage) over [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)'s shared bar, routes keepers into
103	   the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed, a
104	   **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
105	   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
106	   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
107	   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
108	3. **Deletion — the agentless `logs-prune` task**
109	   ([tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs](tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs)), daily, over the same branch: every
110	   capture past `config.retention_days` is removed, on the stamp in its filename alone. What makes
111	   that safe without an agent is the reading window above — the extract run reads from the oldest end
112	   of the branch on every run, so a capture reaches retention having been read. **Unset retention = the
113	   prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).
114	
115	No adoption question over it — `retention_days` stays unset (hidden) by default, which is
116	fail-safe (capture-only). A project that wants the prune active sets `config.retention_days`
117	itself (10 is the recommended floor); nothing else to schedule, since both tasks ride the
118	fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.
119	
120	## Skill-usage metrics — what the mounted skills actually do
121	
122	Mounting a skill only puts its name and one-line description into the session prompt; whether the
123	model ever **loads** it is discretion, and nothing recorded it. So the promotion ladder's
124	skill-vs-prose call had no empirical feedback: a skill whose trigger never fires looked exactly like
125	one that fires daily, and a "skill" that loads in every session (rules wearing a skill's clothes)
126	looked exactly like a genuinely activity-scoped one.
127	
128	The [usage-fold](../claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/README.md) task closes that loop — hourly, agentless, seconds. It
129	counts skill loads **and their denominators** (captures, merges, sessions, user messages, user
130	commands) out of the logs this pack already captures, into
131	`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`: day rows recomputed statelessly inside the raw retention
132	window, week rows appended once past a `foldedThrough` watermark. Denominators are the point — a raw
133	count cannot tell healthy-rare from broken, so the question is loads *against the sessions where that
134	skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied*. Zeros are implicit (a skill with no loads has no
135	key), which is what makes "never loads" visible: diff the file against the repo's mounted skills.
136	
137	Fleet-wide aggregation is deliberately **not** here — the canon knows mechanisms, never repos, so
138	it belongs to the fleet-enforcer repo, the only place that knows who the members are.
139	
140	## Skills
141	
142	Each stage's **method** lives in a skill, so the task doc frames the unattended run and the same
143	method is available to an owner asking in-session. Extract's three are listed above;
144	[**growth-dedup**](skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md) is the dedup stage's — what to prune, strip, or
145	rephrase, the keep-test, and the shrink-only discipline. The pack also bundles
146	[unattended-agents](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md),
147	[generate-project-instructions](skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) and
148	[**writing-tasks**](skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md) — the contract a `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` and
149	its worker are written to: the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the
150	precondition as the only place a task may decide not to run, and how a work item converges. That
151	contract is what the four task checks below judge against, and it is a skill rather than a rule
152	because it is wanted when a task is being written, not carried by every session in every repo.
153	Adoption itself — `adopt-claudinite`, `adopt-pack` and the `adopt-requested-packs` task — is not
154	here: its subject is Claudinite's own surface, not lesson capture.
155	
156	## Rules (`RULES.md`)
157	
158	| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
159	|---|---|---|---|
160	| Changing a local pack automatically | high | complexity | prose: 65 words |
161	| Wanting a job to run in Actions | high | complexity | prose: 55 words + check (`scheduler-workflow-shape`) |
162	
163	## Coded rules
164	
165	| Rule | Kind | What |
166	|---|---|---|
167	| `dedup-prune-integrity` | work-scope ([dedup-integrity.mjs](workRules/dedup-integrity.mjs)) | a dedup edit only removes portable text — never grows a local pack or re-imports a canon rule |
168	| `growth-write-scope` | work-scope ([growth-write-scope.mjs](workRules/growth-write-scope.mjs)) | a capture run (extract, dedup) writes only the repo's own local packs |
169	
170	The capture runs' write surface is the local packs and nothing else — a run improves the repo's
171	**packs**, never the canon it prunes against or the project's own code. `growth-write-scope` is
172	the machine guarantee behind that, keyed on the pinned commit titles of exactly those two runs; the
173	lifecycle's wider-surfaced runs have their own gates (promote writes the canon under `packs/` and
174	`skills/`, certified by canon-curation's `promote-scope`; pack discovery also writes the repo-root
175	declaration that activates the pack it authors).
176	
177	**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
178	an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
179	**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
180	existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
181	**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through a **reviewed** PR (a new pack ships new
182	`.mjs` checks, and a check can break CI — the same reason `prose-to-checks-sweep` is reviewed, and
183	the one place this stage differs from extract). It writes only the repo's own
184	`.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central promote
185	task's job.
186	
187	## Rules expire when the environment moves — revalidation
188	
189	Capture, dedup and conversion all assume a rule is either right or superseded. A third failure mode
190	has no local signal at all: the rule was right, and the **world** changed. A claim that the harness
191	rejects a call in some shape, that the Action's token cannot push a path, that an MCP tool exists —
192	each is a fact about a platform this repo does not control, and when it stops being true nothing
193	here goes red. The prose keeps reading as authoritative, sessions keep obeying it, and the cost
194	lands as a session spent on a route that closed.
195	
196	[rule-revalidation](tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md) is the weekly re-probe. It takes **every**
197	environment-dependent claim in the capture surface — the judgment prose that makes up most of a pack
198	is out of scope, so that set is far smaller than the corpus — **runs** the smallest read-only thing
199	that would distinguish true from false for each, and corrects what the probe contradicts, in a
200	reviewed PR whose body carries the probe evidence, since that is the one thing a reviewer cannot
201	re-derive from the diff. Its scope is the same `pack_paths` config `prose-to-checks-sweep` reads, so
202	a repo names its capture surface once. Covering the whole set every run is what lets the task hold
203	no state between runs: there is no "what did I probe last time" to remember.
204	
205	The dangerous verdict is the one it refuses to reach. An executor session carries the reach its
206	repo's routine was provisioned with, which is not the reach every rule was written under, so a probe
207	that cannot run is logged **unprobed** and the rule is left untouched. Rewriting a rule into "you
208	cannot do X" because one session could not is unfalsifiable afterwards and removes the capability
209	from every future session — which is why an unprobed
210	claim is reported in the run's PR body as explicitly as a corrected one.
211	
212	## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)
213	
214	Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
215	`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
216	procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
217	project's own content;
218	the rest of `.claudinite/` is the **read-only mounted canon** and is never a capture, prune, or
219	promote target. So "a project's local packs" means precisely *everything under
220	`.claudinite/local_packs/`, and nothing else under `.claudinite/`*. This is the normalized capture
221	surface — a structural set the stages read the same way, not a `CLAUDE.md`-graph walk over stray
222	Markdown (a repo with no local packs yet simply has nothing to extract, dedup, or promote here; a
223	project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill).
224	
225	Prefer the strongest mechanism the lesson allows — the **local promotion ladder**, applied at the
226	project's own level: a deterministic rule becomes a **check** whose failure message carries the lesson —
227	a **declared** one in the owning pack's `declared-checks.json` wherever patterns over files can say it,
228	a **rule module** in its `rules` only where they can't — an activity-scoped procedure becomes a **pack
229	skill**, and only what none of those can carry lands as **prose** in a pack's `RULES.md`. A check relieves every session's
230	context completely where prose only relocates it, so capture writes *more checks and less prose*.
231	
232	The stages differ only in *how they read that set*, never in *which set it is*: extract and dedup
233	run against the member repo and read the local packs from the working tree; promote runs centrally
234	and reads the same subtree over the GitHub API (get-file-contents under `.claudinite/local_packs/`).
235	Extract writes into it, promote reads from it, dedup prunes within it — all against the identical,
236	`.claudinite/local_packs/`-rooted set.
237	
238	## The change record: each local pack's own `VERSIONS.md`
239	
240	A canon pack's `VERSIONS.md` carries one row per version bump. A local pack is neither versioned nor
241	distributed, so its `VERSIONS.md` carries the same thing at the only granularity it has: **one row
242	per change automatic work made to it** — a prose rule added or removed, a check created, a rule
243	corrected against a probe or deleted as irrelevant.
244	
245	| Date | Task | Change |
246	|---|---|---|
247	| 2026-08-23 | `growth-extract` | Added: **Restoring source after a see-it-fail mutation** — `git checkout --`, never a `.bak`. |
248	| 2026-08-23 | `prose-to-checks-sweep` | Converted to a check: the entry-point await rule → `pack-discovery-entry-await`. |

# claudinite-growth

Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.

This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.

Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
scheduler (`packs/claudinite-tasks/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:

| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | weekly, when the canon or the project's local packs moved in the week | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | weekly (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |
| `rule-revalidation` ([tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md](tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md)) | weekly | a reviewed PR correcting rules whose environment claim no longer probes true |

(Plus two agentless tasks over the conversation-logs branch: [usage-fold](../claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/README.md) hourly,
described below, and `logs-prune` — retention, [tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs](tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs).)

## Extraction is one task over two sources

`growth-extract` is the whole capture stage, and it runs **three skills** in order:

1. [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) over the window's commits, merged
   PRs and issue discussion;
2. [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) over the logs captured
   from working sessions;
3. [prose-to-checks](skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) over the prose **that run just wrote**, to see
   whether any of it upgrades to a check before the PR opens.

Everything lands in **one** PR, delivered to land where the repo's delivery settings allow
(`packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md`). The two extraction halves used to be two tasks firing in
the same nightly anchor against the same local packs; they share the lesson bar, the promotion ladder
and the dedup surface ([extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)), so the split bought nothing
and cost a second opus dispatch, a second PR, and two runs deduping against a corpus the other was
concurrently writing.

The third step is why the standing `prose-to-checks-sweep` is **weekly**: fresh prose is already
offered a conversion the night it is written, so what the sweep sees is a backlog that moves on a
weekly clock.

A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "claudinite-growth", "config": { "promote": false } }`
— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).

## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in the daily task, retention

The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions**, replacing the old in-session post-merge
lessons pass. Capture and extraction split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session
transcript, so it runs in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only
reads the already-pushed logs, so it is the conversation half of the ordinary `growth-extract`
scheduled task — the logs branch is *in the repo*, so reading it, committing lessons to local packs,
and pruning are plain local git on the working tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the
GitHub MCP tools.

1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
   Right after a merge lands:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
   on, so `test/pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that
   do. **Best effort:** a container reclaimed by timeout never fires it, so nothing depends on it
   having run — every firing enriches the record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only
   behaviour. An `issue-0` log has no issue for the extract to post its exchange
   summary on; nothing else about its lifecycle differs.
   **Unattended sessions capture through the same step, deliberately not through the hook.** A
   scheduled task's executor session ends by having its container reclaimed, which is exactly
   the ending no `SessionEnd` fires on — so the executor runs the engine's runner itself as its
   last step and names its work item in `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE`, which this step uses in
   place of `0`. Those logs therefore file under the task that ran (the item's title
   names `pack/task`), and the work no human watched becomes as countable as the work one did.
2. **The pass — the conversation half of [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)**
   (precondition: a substantive merge; local git on the repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It
   applies the [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) skill (the
   friction signals and the measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and
   token usage) over [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)'s shared bar, routes keepers into
   the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed, a
   **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
3. **Deletion — the agentless `logs-prune` task**
   ([tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs](tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs)), daily, over the same branch: every
   capture past `config.retention_days` is removed, on the stamp in its filename alone. What makes
   that safe without an agent is the reading window above — the extract run reads from the oldest end
   of the branch on every run, so a capture reaches retention having been read. **Unset retention = the
   prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).

No adoption question over it — `retention_days` stays unset (hidden) by default, which is
fail-safe (capture-only). A project that wants the prune active sets `config.retention_days`
itself (10 is the recommended floor); nothing else to schedule, since both tasks ride the
fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.

## Skill-usage metrics — what the mounted skills actually do

Mounting a skill only puts its name and one-line description into the session prompt; whether the
model ever **loads** it is discretion, and nothing recorded it. So the promotion ladder's
skill-vs-prose call had no empirical feedback: a skill whose trigger never fires looked exactly like
one that fires daily, and a "skill" that loads in every session (rules wearing a skill's clothes)
looked exactly like a genuinely activity-scoped one.

The [usage-fold](../claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/README.md) task closes that loop — hourly, agentless, seconds. It
counts skill loads **and their denominators** (captures, merges, sessions, user messages, user
commands) out of the logs this pack already captures, into
`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`: day rows recomputed statelessly inside the raw retention
window, week rows appended once past a `foldedThrough` watermark. Denominators are the point — a raw
count cannot tell healthy-rare from broken, so the question is loads *against the sessions where that
skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied*. Zeros are implicit (a skill with no loads has no
key), which is what makes "never loads" visible: diff the file against the repo's mounted skills.

Fleet-wide aggregation is deliberately **not** here — the canon knows mechanisms, never repos, so
it belongs to the fleet-enforcer repo, the only place that knows who the members are.

## Skills

Each stage's **method** lives in a skill, so the task doc frames the unattended run and the same
method is available to an owner asking in-session. Extract's three are listed above;
[**growth-dedup**](skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md) is the dedup stage's — what to prune, strip, or
rephrase, the keep-test, and the shrink-only discipline. The pack also bundles
[unattended-agents](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md),
[generate-project-instructions](skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) and
[**writing-tasks**](skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md) — the contract a `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` and
its worker are written to: the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the
precondition as the only place a task may decide not to run, and how a work item converges. That
contract is what the four task checks below judge against, and it is a skill rather than a rule
because it is wanted when a task is being written, not carried by every session in every repo.
Adoption itself — `adopt-claudinite`, `adopt-pack` and the `adopt-requested-packs` task — is not
here: its subject is Claudinite's own surface, not lesson capture.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Changing a local pack automatically | high | complexity | prose: 65 words |
| Wanting a job to run in Actions | high | complexity | prose: 55 words + check (`scheduler-workflow-shape`) |

## Coded rules

| Rule | Kind | What |
|---|---|---|
| `dedup-prune-integrity` | work-scope ([dedup-integrity.mjs](workRules/dedup-integrity.mjs)) | a dedup edit only removes portable text — never grows a local pack or re-imports a canon rule |
| `growth-write-scope` | work-scope ([growth-write-scope.mjs](workRules/growth-write-scope.mjs)) | a capture run (extract, dedup) writes only the repo's own local packs |

The capture runs' write surface is the local packs and nothing else — a run improves the repo's
**packs**, never the canon it prunes against or the project's own code. `growth-write-scope` is
the machine guarantee behind that, keyed on the pinned commit titles of exactly those two runs; the
lifecycle's wider-surfaced runs have their own gates (promote writes the canon under `packs/` and
`skills/`, certified by canon-curation's `promote-scope`; pack discovery also writes the repo-root
declaration that activates the pack it authors).

**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through a **reviewed** PR (a new pack ships new
`.mjs` checks, and a check can break CI — the same reason `prose-to-checks-sweep` is reviewed, and
the one place this stage differs from extract). It writes only the repo's own
`.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central promote
task's job.

## Rules expire when the environment moves — revalidation

Capture, dedup and conversion all assume a rule is either right or superseded. A third failure mode
has no local signal at all: the rule was right, and the **world** changed. A claim that the harness
rejects a call in some shape, that the Action's token cannot push a path, that an MCP tool exists —
each is a fact about a platform this repo does not control, and when it stops being true nothing
here goes red. The prose keeps reading as authoritative, sessions keep obeying it, and the cost
lands as a session spent on a route that closed.

[rule-revalidation](tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md) is the weekly re-probe. It takes **every**
environment-dependent claim in the capture surface — the judgment prose that makes up most of a pack
is out of scope, so that set is far smaller than the corpus — **runs** the smallest read-only thing
that would distinguish true from false for each, and corrects what the probe contradicts, in a
reviewed PR whose body carries the probe evidence, since that is the one thing a reviewer cannot
re-derive from the diff. Its scope is the same `pack_paths` config `prose-to-checks-sweep` reads, so
a repo names its capture surface once. Covering the whole set every run is what lets the task hold
no state between runs: there is no "what did I probe last time" to remember.

The dangerous verdict is the one it refuses to reach. An executor session carries the reach its
repo's routine was provisioned with, which is not the reach every rule was written under, so a probe
that cannot run is logged **unprobed** and the rule is left untouched. Rewriting a rule into "you
cannot do X" because one session could not is unfalsifiable afterwards and removes the capability
from every future session — which is why an unprobed
claim is reported in the run's PR body as explicitly as a corrected one.

## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)

Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
project's own content;
the rest of `.claudinite/` is the **read-only mounted canon** and is never a capture, prune, or
promote target. So "a project's local packs" means precisely *everything under
`.claudinite/local_packs/`, and nothing else under `.claudinite/`*. This is the normalized capture
surface — a structural set the stages read the same way, not a `CLAUDE.md`-graph walk over stray
Markdown (a repo with no local packs yet simply has nothing to extract, dedup, or promote here; a
project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill).

Prefer the strongest mechanism the lesson allows — the **local promotion ladder**, applied at the
project's own level: a deterministic rule becomes a **check** whose failure message carries the lesson —
a **declared** one in the owning pack's `declared-checks.json` wherever patterns over files can say it,
a **rule module** in its `rules` only where they can't — an activity-scoped procedure becomes a **pack
skill**, and only what none of those can carry lands as **prose** in a pack's `RULES.md`. A check relieves every session's
context completely where prose only relocates it, so capture writes *more checks and less prose*.

The stages differ only in *how they read that set*, never in *which set it is*: extract and dedup
run against the member repo and read the local packs from the working tree; promote runs centrally
and reads the same subtree over the GitHub API (get-file-contents under `.claudinite/local_packs/`).
Extract writes into it, promote reads from it, dedup prunes within it — all against the identical,
`.claudinite/local_packs/`-rooted set.

## The change record: each local pack's own `VERSIONS.md`

A canon pack's `VERSIONS.md` carries one row per version bump. A local pack is neither versioned nor
distributed, so its `VERSIONS.md` carries the same thing at the only granularity it has: **one row
per change automatic work made to it** — a prose rule added or removed, a check created, a rule
corrected against a probe or deleted as irrelevant.

| Date | Task | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-23 | `growth-extract` | Added: **Restoring source after a see-it-fail mutation** — `git checkout --`, never a `.bak`. |
| 2026-08-23 | `prose-to-checks-sweep` | Converted to a check: the entry-point await rule → `pack-discovery-entry-await`. |

Every growth task writes its own rows, in the same PR as the change they describe, so the record
diffs beside what it records and travels with the pack it is about. A reader looking at a rule and
wondering where it came from is already in the directory.

This is the growth lifecycle's **whole** record: no growth task keeps a standing tracker issue. An
issue body is rewritten in place with no history, sits outside the PR that made the change, and is
one sweep away from being closed as stale — none of which is true of a tracked file. A run that
changed nothing writes no row at all: the file logs what happened to the pack, never that a run
happened.

`seedRepoLocalPack` creates the file empty at adoption, so no task has to invent it.

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dedup-prune-integrity` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `growth-write-scope` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `in-session-github-access` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `routine-structure` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `task-declaration-matches-folder` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-md-only-when-agentic` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-phase-discipline` | medium | complexity | check: advisory |

The last five are the **task contract** ([the writing-tasks skill](skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md)), which
lives here because it judges whether a task is *written* correctly — authoring, the subject of this
pack — and not whether Claudinite is *working* in the repo. Relevance-first: all five are inert until
the repo carries a `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` of its own.

- `task-declaration-matches-folder` — a declaration disagrees with its folder: discovery drops it into `errors` and every run keeps reporting healthy without it.
- `task-md-only-when-agentic` — an agentless task carries a `task.md`, which the corpus reads as "an agent runs here": prose no session will ever open, judged by the routine contract and named by every work item as the file the run is about.
- `task-phase-discipline` — a task decides not to run after its precondition already said run, hiding the decision from the run records.

{"number":1398,"title":"Label scheme PR 4: sweep the writer-facing vocabulary","body":"The last unbuilt box of #1119's review pass.

## Half 1 — product-wiki's gate — nothing to do

The plan said the gate should read its own approval-parked item instead of a labeled PR. `c0dd572` (#1257, closing #1256) got there first, and by a better route: the `prs` collector resolves each open PR's changed paths, and the precondition declines on a pending `product-wiki/` change in **any** open PR — so a human's wiki edit in flight gates the round too, which an item-marker read never would. `product-wiki-growth` is gone and `prs.open[].labels` went with it. Verified against the file, not the commit message.

## Half 2 — the sweep

#1385 swept the three briefs it touched. What it did not reach is every other document an agent reads **at run time** that still asks for the retired pair — `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-`. A park has been one label since `a7e49ed0`, so a brief still asking for two is asking for the torn state §6.2's repair rule exists to clean up.

Swept: `writing-tasks` (which also still named `task:obsolete` as the never-ran terminal, now `task:status:rejected`), the `update` brief and the updates README, the `fleet-digest`, `ci-performance` and `growth-dedup` briefs, sheepdog's README and its four task READMEs, `task-phase-discipline`'s remedy line, and the lines in `tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` that state today's mechanism in the pair form.

Deliberately **not** swept, each because the legacy spelling is the point there:

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md` — the retired slot mechanism's instructions, kept for routines nobody has repointed. Its `agent-running` / `needs-human` vocabulary is that scheme's, and rewriting it would break the sessions it is kept for.
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md`, `docs/per-project-scheduling/*`, `docs/task-code-work/DESIGN.md`, `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` — records of play-throughs and superseded schemes.
- DESIGN §4's legacy decode table and §15's decision records — the decode map is permanent, and a decision record says what was decided when.
- every `VERSIONS.md`; and `on_interrupt: 'requeue' | 'needs-human'`, a declaration value rather than a label (its one prose mention is now quoted as the value it is).

## The assurance, written first

`vocabulary.test.mjs` gains two scans — over pack prose and over the check catalogs' agent-facing fields — built from the `LEGACY_*` constants rather than a hand-copied list, and reading the tracked tree so a brief added later is covered without being listed. Both failed on `main` (12 offending briefs, one remedy) before any file was touched.

## One thing this leaves open, deliberately

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/terminals.mjs` returns `label: NEEDS_HUMAN` and `tasks/update/worker.mjs` applies it — to the update **PR**, not to a work item. That is a live write of the bare legacy label, but it is code and a cross-repo convention rather than prose, so it is out of this PR's scope. Filed as #1399.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/    the two vocabulary scans (test only — nothing vendored changes)
packs/claudinite-growth/   writing-tasks' terminal and park spellings; the
                           task-phase-discipline remedy. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/ the update brief's park section and the updates README.
                           Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/ the pack README and four task READMEs say a failed
                           sweep parks. Version bumped.
packs/basics/              the ci-performance brief's missing-input park. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the fleet-digest brief's missing-input park. Version bumped.
docs/                      tasks-dispatch DESIGN's live statements only.
```

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2728 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — clean.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 87 advisory**, the same count `main` carries.

Closes #1395

{"number":1422,"title":"product-wiki: bundle the /explore-link skill","body":"Closes #1421

The pack grew its wikis on one lane only — the weekly `wiki-growth` pass, which picks its own targets from each page's `## Open questions`. `/explore-link` is the other lane: the owner hands over a **source**, and the run's judgment is which existing wiki page it feeds, what the four axes take out of it, and what it turns out not to say.

## What the skill carries

{"number":1397,"title":"Retire the fleet-digest task and the digests panel","body":"The fleet morning brief is no longer wanted. `missingbulb/Shepherd` — the only deployment writing the series — is deleting its `digests/` folder (missingbulb/Shepherd#296), and the task is not gated on any config, so as long as it ships in the pack it writes the folder back the next morning.

So the producer goes, and with it the only thing that read its output. Keeping the panel would leave a `digestsRepo` key promising a file nothing writes.

**Removed**

- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/tasks/fleet-digest/` — the task, its worker, the fleet enumeration it brought over from `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`, and the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` handover step it rendered into adoption.
- Both of its checks, `digest-plain-text` and `dated-fixture-collision`. `descriptor-usable` is now the pack's only one.
- The fleet page's morning-brief panel, `digest.mjs` behind it, its markup and CSS, and the `digestsRepo` / `digestsPath` / `digest` config keys.
- The `digests` figure in `fleetBenefits`, and the `dashboard-digest` rehearsal fixture — it existed to prove those two blocking checks converge green in a member, and `dashboard-contributor` already covers the plain page-only shape.

**Consumer safety.** No migration record:

- A member's standing `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest` item closes itself through the queue's existing orphan reap (`scheduler-run.mjs` — "a standing item whose task is gone closes").
- `loadConfig` spreads the deployment's `dashboard.config.json` over the defaults, so a leftover `digestsRepo` is ignored rather than rejected; nothing validates pack config against a key list either, so a leftover `digest` block on a declaration is inert.

**Verification.** Full canon suite green (2,666 pass / 0 fail), `check_the_world` 0 blocking, `check_the_work` clean, rebased on current `main`.

Closes #1392

{"number":1419,"title":"Promote a lesson from Shepherd's local pack","body":"Refs #99. `canon-curation/growth-promote` run over `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s local pack — the only target named in #1417's Context (its local pack changed since the prior run, #1372/2026-08-26; the rest of the pack's content was already read and dedup-checked by earlier runs).

**One prose addition** (`packs/basics/RULES.md`, Working discipline) — a judgment/process rule with no static repo signature:

- **Shepherd** → `basics/RULES.md` — declaring a repo the new home of a role a retiring predecessor already filled (Shepherd's own Sheepdog-to-Shepherd preferences-store handoff, generalized) means copying the predecessor's *actual content* in the same change as the declaration, not the declaration alone — and acting on a gap your own tooling already surfaced rather than leaving it for a human to notice.

Version bumped: `basics` 60827.2 → 60829.1.

**Not a duplicate of the still-open #1157's "Retiring a system by folding its function into another" bullet** (also from Shepherd, still unmerged): that rule is about a *regenerable* artifact — verifying the generator moved, not just its output. This one is about a *declared role* (a store nothing regenerates) — verifying the content moved, not just the declaration. Related theme, different failure mode; kept as its own bullet rather than folded, since conflating the two would blur a concrete lesson into a vaguer one.

Verified: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2755/2755 green (unshallowed the checkout first; `rule-index.test.mjs`'s word-count/label-length checks caught the README row on the first pass — fixed in this branch). `check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 86 advisory, none touching the files this PR changes.

Two findings from the sim conversion that refine the plan (appended, nothing above changes):
- **One-issue decline semantics**: a refused request's terminal status stands on the *open* issue (the run's verdict is not the issue's validity); a closed or gone issue closes/removes its item with it. The engine's implement-request path must mirror this.

2026-08-21: PRs 1 and 2 are built, in #1138 — as two commits on one branch, since the session could only push to its designated branch. PR 3 is deliberately not there: its merge is gated on the fleet force that follows 1–2.

Three things the build settled, appended:

- **Execution step 1's contingency does not apply.** The stubs are converge-delivered, not copied-once: `convergeWiring` rewrites both workflow files from the vendored stubs whole (`convergeExecutorWorkflow` → `writeWorkflow`). The real lag is that `.github/workflows/` lands as a PR somebody merges, so a member spends a window running the old copy against the new engine — which costs a label event, never work, because the hourly scheduler dispatch is the guaranteed delivery. That window is now a rehearsal fixture shape rather than an assumption.
- **`consumer-safe-change` watched only the scheduler stub.** The executor's is vendored just as verbatim, and a workflow trigger names label strings literally — exactly the surface this migration has to carry members across. Widened.
- **The `Task:` targeting field landed; the `add-packs` fold did not.** The field is in and recorded as DESIGN §16.12. Folding `add-packs` onto it rewrites a cross-repo contract and has one failure mode that needs a decision rather than a guess: the enforcer writes into a member over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and a member whose mark label does not exist yet refuses that write and runs nothing, where today's dispatch-and-wake protocol is robust to it. Everything the fold needs on the member side is in place.

2026-08-21, later: the `add-packs` fold landed in #1138 (owner's call: the enforcer creates the mark in the member, then applies it), and PR 3 is built in #1152, stacked on #1138 and **not to be merged before execution step 1**.

Appended, since both settled something the plan left open:

- **The fold needed a serializer nobody had noticed.** Two work lists in one member (REQUESTED and SUSPECTED) are two items of one task, and nothing serializes them — their titles differ, so the same-title mutex does not see them, and two sessions editing one `.claudinite-checks.json` is two conflicting PRs. The enforcer names the member's other open list in `Blocked-by:`, so the queue's own dependency field does the queueing. The dispatch that remains is latency, not delivery: an ordinary scheduler run, and a member that refuses it adopts on its own next hour, so an unfired member no longer fails the sweep.
- **`pack-version-bumped` cannot see a stacked bump.** It compares against `main`, so a pack edited in both #1138 and #1152 looks bumped when the second PR's edits actually ride a version the first already delivered — they would reach nobody. `basics` and `claudinite-dashboard` carry a second bump in #1152 for that reason. Worth a check of its own if stacked PRs become normal here.

Ran the fleet-wide label cleanup pass this issue's tail is waiting on, with GitHub issue read+write on all 14 active members. **Nothing was relabelled and no label was deleted** — three separate blockers, each read rather than assumed. Reporting all of it.

## How the fleet reads were made

The previous attempt on #1154 parked because "this session's GitHub access is scoped to `missingbulb/Claudinite` only". That is fixable from inside a session: `add_repo` (Claude Code Remote) widens this session's GitHub scope, and it did — all 14 members attached, and `list_issues`/`issue_read` against each returned normally. Fleet enumeration re-derived from `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` (`coverage.folding`, 14 repos incl. the canon; `coverage.dormant` = HelloWorldFlutterApp, gRatio, no mount). No read was refused, and no sweep came back empty or rate-limited.

## 1. #1154's remaining Verify leg — PASSES

No open `[claudinite-work]` item parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z names a label, a status, or a missing label as its cause. Read the park comments directly on Shepherd #205, ClaudiniteCanary #264, ClaudiniteWebsite #321, EdFringeNow #491, GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050, MissingBulbWebsite #240, TLDR #367, VascularColoring #258, hitbut #135 — spanning every member with a post-cutoff park and all four park kinds. The causes are four, none of them the label scheme:

- `converge-item.mjs` cannot authenticate — the dispatched session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a proxy sentinel (401/403 "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). This is the dominant cause, already tracked as #1133, #1149 and #1374.
- `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` not set (ClaudiniteCanary #264, `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`).
- `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` (GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050).
- No readable `.claudinite-settings.json`, status 404 (Shepherd #205).

Worth naming explicitly, because it reads like a counter-example and is not one: several of these items are **still wearing `task:agent`** (EdFringeNow #491, TLDR #367, MissingBulbWebsite #240, ClaudiniteWebsite #321). That label is the *residue* of a convergence that could not run — each session deliberately declined to hand-roll the swap — not the cause of the park. The janitor then escalated them on the 3h stale-agent rule. The decode reached them fine.

## 2. #1152 CANNOT be merged — its step-4 preconditions are false

Per #1154's playbook step 4, confirmed before merging rather than after. Two of the four conditions fail:

| Condition | Read |
|---|---|
| open | ✅ open, not draft |
| base is `main` | ✅ base `main` @ `f71ef81` |
| checks green | ⚠️ one check run, `test-and-conformance` success — but from **2026-08-21T11:33**, and `main` has taken **52 commits** since |
| GitHub reports it mergeable | ❌ **`mergeable_state: "dirty"`** |

Verified independently of the API: after `git fetch --unshallow`, `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/claude/claudinite-issue-1119-pr3-flip` returns **11 content conflicts** —

```
packs/basics/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-dashboard/{fleet,pack,ui,view-repo}.mjs
packs/claudinite-growth/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/queue/{executor-loop,scheduler-run,vocabulary}.test.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/tasks/task-janitor-queue-sweep.test.mjs
```

And the deeper problem: the PR's own body describes editing `engine/scheduler/queue/`. **That directory no longer exists on `main`** — the queue moved into `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` with the #1317 extraction. Git's rename detection still follows the flip onto the new paths, so the change is recoverable, but this is not a rebase-and-merge; it is a re-land onto a surface that moved underneath it, and the six-day-old green covers neither the new layout nor the 52 intervening commits.

**Not merged. #1154 left open**, and re-parked from `task:needs-human-action` to `task:needs-human-decision` — the enumeration blocker its old park named is gone, and what is left is a choice (re-land the flip on the moved layout, or supersede #1152) rather than a mechanical action.

## 3. The relabel and the deletions are both blocked — and the deletions would not have held anyway

**Relabel (closed issues, legacy → canonical): not performed.** The write-side flip has not merged, so no member's stamp can yet carry it; relabelling now just re-dirties as the still-legacy engine keeps writing legacy spellings. This is the ordering this issue's own plan sets, and it holds.

**Deleting the legacy label *definitions*: would be undone within a day, on every member.** `QUEUE_LABELS` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs:323` still lists every legacy name — `task:blocked`, `task:ready`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`, `needs-human`, all four `task:needs-human-*`, `task:done`, `task:obsolete` — and `ensureLabels(gh, repo, QUEUE_LABELS)` runs from `scheduler-run.mjs:671,794`, `executor.mjs:618`, `create-work-item.mjs:97` and the janitor's `queue-sweep.mjs:53`. Every scheduler cycle in every member re-creates any of them that is missing. #1152 does not change this — its own body is explicit: *"They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it."*

So deleting the definitions is not the tail of this migration; **dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` is**, and that is a separate change gated on 4(b) below reaching zero.

## 4. The two reads other issues are waiting on

### (a) For #1382 — open `[claudinite-task]` issues: **NOT zero. Three, across two members.**

- **EdFringeNow** — #363 `[claudinite-task] edfringe/refresh-tickets d2026-08-15`, #359 `[claudinite-task] grow_with_claudinite/growth-extract d2026-08-15`
- **VascularColoring** — #109 `[claudinite-task] core/update d2026-08-15~f31916551918` (also wears `escalation:apply-stage`)
- All other 12 members, canon included: **zero**.

Read from every open issue title in all 14 repos (not a search). #1382's removal is gated: deleting `ready-for-agent` / `ready-for-agent-fleet` / `agent-running` would strip them off these three, and deleting the janitor's two dispatch rules abandons them.

### (b) For this issue's tail — open work items still wearing a legacy status spelling: **NOT zero. ~176, on all 14 members.**

| Member | open items wearing a legacy status | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Claudinite | 33 | incl. #1086 also on `task:agent` |
| hitbut | 24 | all `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-action` |
| ClaudiniteCanary | 22 | incl. #133 `task:agent` |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | 15 | incl. #321 `task:agent` |
| VascularColoring | 14 | incl. #109, a `[claudinite-task]` |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | 12 | incl. #1076 `task:agent` |
| MissingBulbWebsite | 12 | |
| EdFringeNow | 11 | incl. #363, #359, `[claudinite-task]`s |
| CrosswordChat | 7 | |
| LaughCounter | 7 | |
| Shepherd | 6 | |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | 6 | |
| TLDR | 6 | |
| WIP | 1 | |

Every one of these is the `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-` pair, four are `task:agent`, and a long tail also carries `origin:schedule`. **The decode map's legacy entries cannot leave the engine.** They are not draining on their own either: the drain depends on convergence, and convergence is exactly what is broken fleet-wide (#1133 / #1149 / #1374). Until an item can converge, the legacy-wearing population grows rather than shrinks.

## What this leaves

The tail of this migration is blocked behind three things, in order:

1. **Convergence has to work** (#1149 / #1374). Nothing drains until it does, so 4(b) cannot reach zero.
2. **#1152 has to be re-landed** on the post-#1317 layout, re-verified against current `main` — a branch's own green never covers the whole-tree aggregate.
3. **Then** the closed-issue relabel, and only after that, dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` — which is what actually retires the definitions.

Not closing this issue, not editing its body.

**PR 3 has merged** — `a7e49ed0`, [#1385](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1385), not #1152. #1152 is closed: it was `dirty` with 11 conflicts and written against `engine/scheduler/queue/`, which #1317 moved. #1385 re-lands the same flip on the current layout, rebased onto `3541d6a` and verified there — 2722 tests pass, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking / 87 advisory, identical to `origin/main` in a clean worktree.

One thing the re-land caught that the original branch could not have: `packs/claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` postdate #1152 and used `NEEDS_HUMAN` as a **state key**, the same way `fleet.mjs` and `ui.mjs` did. Merged as-was, both would have compared `stateOf()`'s output against a label the engine no longer writes — no error, no failing test, and **zero parked items counted on both dashboards**. They move to `PARKED` with the rest, and `model.mjs` stops re-exporting the deprecated constant so the page side cannot reach for it again.

**Execution step 2 remains**, and is now filed as its own verification: [#1391](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1391), attached here as a sub-issue. It waits on ClaudiniteCanary's stamp reaching `packVersions.claudinite-tasks` ≥ `60827.3`, then reads that member's own issues to confirm a fresh scheduler cycle files items wearing exactly one `task:status:*`, one `task:origin:*`, and no legacy spelling. Retries daily until live. Forcing `fleet-baseline` with `follow` would bring that moment forward; the nightly converge gets there on its own otherwise.

**A correction to what I wrote earlier today.** My first comment framed "dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS`" as this migration's real tail. This issue's own body says otherwise, and it is right: *"Legacy label definitions are never deleted (deleting a label strips it from closed issues — stored data); the decode map is permanent."* So the label deletions I was asked to make are not merely blocked or futile against the nightly ensure pass — they were never part of the plan, and doing them would destroy stored data on closed issues fleet-wide. The genuine tail is the two items already in the body: removing legacy spellings from the stub triggers once no fielded engine writes them, and marking the legacy label series historical wherever counts are folded.

Ran the fleet-wide label cleanup pass this issue's tail is waiting on, with GitHub issue read+write on all 14 active members. **Nothing was relabelled and no label was deleted** — three separate blockers, each read rather than assumed. Reporting all of it.

## How the fleet reads were made

The previous attempt on #1154 parked because "this session's GitHub access is scoped to `missingbulb/Claudinite` only". That is fixable from inside a session: `add_repo` (Claude Code Remote) widens this session's GitHub scope, and it did — all 14 members attached, and `list_issues`/`issue_read` against each returned normally. Fleet enumeration re-derived from `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` (`coverage.folding`, 14 repos incl. the canon; `coverage.dormant` = HelloWorldFlutterApp, gRatio, no mount). No read was refused, and no sweep came back empty or rate-limited.

## 1. #1154's remaining Verify leg — PASSES

No open `[claudinite-work]` item parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z names a label, a status, or a missing label as its cause. Read the park comments directly on Shepherd #205, ClaudiniteCanary #264, ClaudiniteWebsite #321, EdFringeNow #491, GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050, MissingBulbWebsite #240, TLDR #367, VascularColoring #258, hitbut #135 — spanning every member with a post-cutoff park and all four park kinds. The causes are four, none of them the label scheme:

- `converge-item.mjs` cannot authenticate — the dispatched session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a proxy sentinel (401/403 "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). This is the dominant cause, already tracked as #1133, #1149 and #1374.
- `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` not set (ClaudiniteCanary #264, `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`).
- `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` (GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050).
- No readable `.claudinite-settings.json`, status 404 (Shepherd #205).

Worth naming explicitly, because it reads like a counter-example and is not one: several of these items are **still wearing `task:agent`** (EdFringeNow #491, TLDR #367, MissingBulbWebsite #240, ClaudiniteWebsite #321). That label is the *residue* of a convergence that could not run — each session deliberately declined to hand-roll the swap — not the cause of the park. The janitor then escalated them on the 3h stale-agent rule. The decode reached them fine.

## 2. #1152 CANNOT be merged — its step-4 preconditions are false

Per #1154's playbook step 4, confirmed before merging rather than after. Two of the four conditions fail:

| Condition | Read |
|---|---|
| open | ✅ open, not draft |
| base is `main` | ✅ base `main` @ `f71ef81` |
| checks green | ⚠️ one check run, `test-and-conformance` success — but from **2026-08-21T11:33**, and `main` has taken **52 commits** since |
| GitHub reports it mergeable | ❌ **`mergeable_state: "dirty"`** |

Verified independently of the API: after `git fetch --unshallow`, `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/claude/claudinite-issue-1119-pr3-flip` returns **11 content conflicts** —

```
packs/basics/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-dashboard/{fleet,pack,ui,view-repo}.mjs
packs/claudinite-growth/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/queue/{executor-loop,scheduler-run,vocabulary}.test.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/tasks/task-janitor-queue-sweep.test.mjs
```

And the deeper problem: the PR's own body describes editing `engine/scheduler/queue/`. **That directory no longer exists on `main`** — the queue moved into `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` with the #1317 extraction. Git's rename detection still follows the flip onto the new paths, so the change is recoverable, but this is not a rebase-and-merge; it is a re-land onto a surface that moved underneath it, and the six-day-old green covers neither the new layout nor the 52 intervening commits.

**Not merged. #1154 left open**, and re-parked from `task:needs-human-action` to `task:needs-human-decision` — the enumeration blocker its old park named is gone, and what is left is a choice (re-land the flip on the moved layout, or supersede #1152) rather than a mechanical action.

## 3. The relabel and the deletions are both blocked — and the deletions would not have held anyway

**Relabel (closed issues, legacy → canonical): not performed.** The write-side flip has not merged, so no member's stamp can yet carry it; relabelling now just re-dirties as the still-legacy engine keeps writing legacy spellings. This is the ordering this issue's own plan sets, and it holds.

**Deleting the legacy label *definitions*: would be undone within a day, on every member.** `QUEUE_LABELS` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs:323` still lists every legacy name — `task:blocked`, `task:ready`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`, `needs-human`, all four `task:needs-human-*`, `task:done`, `task:obsolete` — and `ensureLabels(gh, repo, QUEUE_LABELS)` runs from `scheduler-run.mjs:671,794`, `executor.mjs:618`, `create-work-item.mjs:97` and the janitor's `queue-sweep.mjs:53`. Every scheduler cycle in every member re-creates any of them that is missing. #1152 does not change this — its own body is explicit: *"They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it."*

So deleting the definitions is not the tail of this migration; **dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` is**, and that is a separate change gated on 4(b) below reaching zero.

## 4. The two reads other issues are waiting on

### (a) For #1382 — open `[claudinite-task]` issues: **NOT zero. Three, across two members.**

- **EdFringeNow** — #363 `[claudinite-task] edfringe/refresh-tickets d2026-08-15`, #359 `[claudinite-task] grow_with_claudinite/growth-extract d2026-08-15`

Until an item can converge, the legacy-wearing population grows rather than shrinks.

## What this leaves

The tail of this migration is blocked behind three things, in order:

1. **Convergence has to work** (#1149 / #1374). Nothing drains until it does, so 4(b) cannot reach zero.
2. **#1152 has to be re-landed** on the post-#1317 layout, re-verified against current `main` — a branch's own green never covers the whole-tree aggregate.
3. **Then** the closed-issue relabel, and only after that, dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` — which is what actually retires the definitions.

{"number":1400,"title":"A local pack declaring `since` wedges a member whose engine predates it","body":"Introduced by #1379, found while filing its verification. **The mechanics below are corrected from the original filing — that version claimed "the pack fails to load", which is not what happens.**

## Why it throws at all

`validateSpecKeys` is deliberate, and the reason is in the module header: *"an unknown key is an authoring error (a typo'd key would otherwise assert nothing, silently)"*. A declaration is data with no compiler behind it — write `scanFile` for `scanFiles`, or `matchLine` for `matchLines`, and the check quietly asserts nothing and reads green forever. That is the corpus's most-repeated failure shape (*a check that matches nothing reads as live*), so failing loud on an unknown key is load-bearing, not incidental strictness.

The asymmetry is that compatibility runs one way only. `normalizeLegacySpellings` maps **old** spellings onto today's — an old declaration read by a new engine is fine, permanently. Nothing handles the reverse: a **new** declaration read by an old engine.

## What actually happens

1. `patternRule` throws on the unknown key.
2. `declaredChecksIn` (`engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs:98`) **catches** it, records a load fault, and returns `[]`. The pack still loads — but **every declaration in that file is dropped**, not just the offending one.
3. `probePackManifests` (`engine/selftest.mjs:111`) sees a non-empty `loaded.errors` and **fails** the `pack-manifests` probe.
4. The converge gates on the self-test: red → the update PR is left open at `needs-human` and does not merge.
5. Separately, `check_the_world` turns the same fault into a **blocking** `config` finding.

So it is loud rather than silent — which is the saving grace, and clearly intended. But the wedge survives: the member cannot converge onto the engine release that would make `since` a valid key, because the converge is gated on a self-test that the invalid key is failing. A human has to delete the key by hand.

## The exposure

Narrow. Nothing in the canon declares `since`, so no member is at risk from the canon side. It needs a member's own growth run to write one into its local pack while that member still holds an engine predating #1379 — the pack lane and the engine lane converge on separate cycles, and `ENGINE_VERSION` was not bumped (it advances by release), so there is no version for `claudinite-growth`'s `minEngineVersion` to point at.

## What "done" looks like

One of, decided deliberately:

- **A forward-compatible key lane.** Keep throwing on a key the engine cannot place, but carve out keys reserved for exactly this — a declaration may carry a key a newer engine knows without an older one dropping the whole file. This is the general fix; the skew will recur with the next vocabulary addition.
- **Or gate the prose.** Bump `ENGINE_VERSION` for a release carrying `since` and raise `claudinite-growth`'s `minEngineVersion` to it, so a member cannot hold the instruction without the vocabulary. Narrower, and pays only for this one key.

Worth deciding alongside either: **one bad declaration currently drops every rule in its file.** That is a large blast radius for a typo, and the two behaviours share a cause.

Whichever is chosen, a rehearsal fixture should pin it: a member on the older engine, holding a local pack whose `declared-checks.json` carries `since`, converging green.
